title: Weaker forms of choice: countable choice and dependent choice

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 30 and 37–38 (§6, Exercise 6.9; §8.1, fragments of choice and AC ⇒ DC ⇒ ACω)

based_on.title: Axiomatic Set Theory
based_on.pages: 165–168 (Appendix C, Definition C.7, Propositions C.8–C.9, and Theorem C.10, implication (i) ⇒ (iii); proof typos repaired)

summary: Compare countable and successive selections, and explain their consequences for infinity and countable unions.
abstract: Countable choice lets us choose one element from each set in a sequence of nonempty sets. Dependent choice lets us make infinitely many successive selections, even when the available options depend on earlier selections. The full axiom of choice implies dependent choice, which in turn implies countable choice. Countable choice already guarantees that every infinite set contains infinitely many distinct elements that can be listed in a sequence, and that a countable union of countable sets is countable. When a given rule specifies each next element, no additional choice assumption is needed to construct the sequence.
